q: When an Architect enters into a contract with the Owner to perform Comprehensive Architectural Services, what dual role does he typically assume?
o: Project Manager (PM) and Construction Manager (CM), effectively the overall coordinator
Bank consultant and Real Estate Consultant
n: Sec. 3.1.1 states that by the nature of CAS, the Architect assumes the dual role of PM and CM, or effectively the overall coordinator whose functions are outlined under this SPP. (Source: SPP Document 206, Sec. 3.1.1)

q: Under Project Management's Pre-Construction Phase (Sec. 2.2.1), when should the PM begin conducting regular consultations with the Owner, Architects, and Engineers?
o: As early as during the design development phase, perhaps even concurrently with the Architect's commission
Only after the building permit is issued
n: Sec. 2.2.1 states the PM should conduct regular consultations as early as the design development phase, possibly even concurrently with the Architect's commission. (Source: SPP Document 206, Sec. 2.2.1)

q: Situational: A Project Manager on a large development is asked to describe his primary responsibility to the Owner. According to SPP 206 Sec. 3.2.2(e), how should he correctly characterize it?
o: Sole legal liability for all contractor defects
The exercise of overall cost control — planning, programming, and monitoring activities, and advising on material costs and construction methods
Design authorship over the architectural plans
n: Sec. 3.2.2(e) states the PM's primary responsibility is the exercise of overall cost control; he plans, programs, and monitors activities, and acts as an adviser on material costs and construction methods. (Source: SPP Document 206, Sec. 3.2.2(e))

q: Which of the following is listed among the Pre-Design Services under SPP 206 Sec. 2.1.1?
n: Value Management (item j) appears in the Pre-Design Services list; the Schematic Design and Bidding/Negotiation phases belong to Regular Design Services (Sec. 2.1.2), and Building Testing and Commissioning belongs to Specialized Architectural Services (Sec. 2.1.3). (Source: SPP Document 206, Sec. 2.1.1)

q: Post-Construction Services, cross-referenced to SPP Document 205, include which two items under SPP 206?
o: Building and Facilities Administration, and Post-Construction Evaluation
Value Management and Design Brief Preparation
n: Sec. 2.1.5 lists Building and Facilities Administration and Post-Construction Evaluation as the components of Post-Construction Services (SPP Document 205). (Source: SPP Document 206, Sec. 2.1.5)

q: Which of the following professionals is explicitly listed in SPP 206 Sec. 3.1.2 as someone the Architect may include in a CAS team?
n: Sec. 3.1.2's list of team members includes Architects, Engineers, Market Analysts, Accountants, General Contractors, Real Estate Consultants, Sociologists, Planners, Bankers, and Lawyers — Lawyers being explicitly named. (Source: SPP Document 206, Sec. 3.1.2)

q: SPP Document 206 replaces which earlier issuance?
n: The document's header states it is 'replacing the 1979 UAP Doc. 206.' (Source: SPP Document 206, Title/Header)

q: In the Owner-Architect-Engineer-Contractor Team Approach under SPP 206, who is responsible for the respective engineering plans?
n: Sec. 3.2.2(b) assigns responsibility for respective engineering plans to the Engineers. (Source: SPP Document 206, Sec. 3.2.2(b))

q: Under SPP 206, Construction Services are divided into which two components?
o: Fulltime Supervision Services (SPP Doc. 204-A) and Construction Management Services (SPP Doc. 204-B)
Site Development Planning and Urban Design
n: Sec. 2.1.4 divides Construction Services into Fulltime Supervision Services (SPP Document 204-A) and Construction Management Services (SPP Document 204-B). (Source: SPP Document 206, Sec. 2.1.4)

q: Specialized Architectural Services, as enumerated in SPP 206 Sec. 2.1.3, are cross-referenced to which SPP document?
n: Sec. 2.1.3 cross-references the long list of Specialized Architectural Services (Architectural Interiors, Acoustic Design, Forensic Architecture, etc.) to SPP Document 203. (Source: SPP Document 206, Sec. 2.1.3)

q: Because the Architect must properly assist and serve the Client under CAS, what additional requirement does SPP 206 place on the Architect?
o: The Architect must personally perform every specialized service
The Architect must waive supervision fees
The Architect must also be a licensed engineer
The Architect must be knowledgeable in other fields in addition to building design
n: Sec. 1.1.3 notes that to properly assist and serve the Client, the Architect has to be knowledgeable in other fields in addition to building design. (Source: SPP Document 206, Sec. 1.1.3)

q: Overall, what best characterizes the relationship between SPP Document 206 and SPP Documents 201, 202, 203, 204, and 205?
o: SPP 206 bundles/coordinates them as the components (Pre-design, Regular Design, Specialized, Construction, Post-Construction) of Comprehensive Architectural Services, cross-referencing each for its detailed scope
They have no relationship — SPP 206 is a wholly independent standard
SPP 206 only cross-references SPP 202 and no other document
SPP 206 supersedes and repeals all of them
n: Throughout Sec. 2.1, SPP 206 organizes the whole range of CAS by cross-referencing SPP Documents 201 (Pre-Design), 202 (Regular Design), 203 (Specialized), 204-A/204-B (Construction), and 205 (Post-Construction) for the detailed scope of each component service. (Source: SPP Document 206, Sec. 2.1)

q: Does the presence of a Project Manager relieve the designers and contractors of their normal duties and responsibilities?
o: Yes, the PM fully assumes all design and construction liability
Only the contractor's duties are relieved
No — the PM complements the functions of the Architects, Engineers, and Contractors without relieving them of their respective duties
Only the engineer's duties are relieved
n: Sec. 1.2.3 clarifies that the PM's presence does not relieve designers and contractors of their normal duties; the PM complements their functions. (Source: SPP Document 206, Sec. 1.2.3)

q: If the Project Manager (PM) also serves as Construction Manager (CM) to oversee time, cost, and quality control during construction, what governs the services he must provide?
n: Sec. 2.2.2 provides that a PM who also serves as CM must provide the services detailed under SPP Documents 204-A and/or 204-B. (Source: SPP Document 206, Sec. 2.2.2)

q: Which SPP Document immediately follows SPP Document 206 in the numbering sequence, and what does it cover?
o: SPP Document 204, on Fulltime Supervision Services
n: The page immediately following SPP Document 206 in the 2010 SPP compilation begins the Standard of Professional Practice on Design-Build Services, SPP Document 207. (Source: SPP Document 206 / SPP Document 207 (adjoining document))

q: Under Comprehensive Architectural Services, what is the role of the Architect described as?
o: The prime professional who functions as creator, author, and coordinator of the building design that becomes the basis for the project's construction
An employee of the general contractor
A subordinate consultant to the Project Manager
A purely advisory role with no design responsibility
n: SPP 206 Sec. 1.1.3 states the Architect is the prime professional, functioning as creator, author, and coordinator of the building design which becomes the basis for the construction of the project. (Source: SPP Document 206, Sec. 1.1.3)

q: What historical development led the architectural profession to adopt Comprehensive Architectural Services (CAS)?
o: The realization that continuity of services related to design and construction is necessary to execute a completely viable project
The abolition of the 'basic services' concept by the PRC
A government mandate under the Local Government Code
A requirement imposed by foreign lending institutions
n: SPP 206 explains that the profession transitioned from providing only 'basic' and 'additional' services to a comprehensive nature because continuity of design- and construction-related services was found necessary for a completely viable project. (Source: SPP Document 206, Sec. 1.1.1)

q: Situational: An Architect performing Comprehensive Architectural Services needs specialized input on market feasibility and financing structures for a large mixed-use project, beyond his own staff's expertise. Per SPP 206 Sec. 3.1.2, what is his proper course of action?
o: Expand the use of his own staff capability as needed, or form/hire a team of other professionals such as Market Analysts, Accountants, and Bankers
Delegate the entire project to the Contractor
Refuse the commission since only the Architect may perform any service
n: Sec. 3.1.2 allows the Architect to make full use of his own staff, expanding capability as needed, or to form a team of other professionals — Architects, Engineers, Market Analysts, Accountants, General Contractors, Real Estate Consultants, Sociologists, Planners, Bankers, and Lawyers. (Source: SPP Document 206, Sec. 3.1.2)

q: Situational: An Owner hires a Project Manager (PM) for a project. Per SPP 206 Sec. 3.2.1, what are the PM's options regarding the Construction Manager (CM) role?
o: The PM may hire the CM (paid by the PM or directly by the Owner on salary or a percentage of construction cost), or the PM may serve as CM himself
The CM must always be a government agency
The Owner must always personally serve as CM
The PM has no authority over CM selection at all
n: Sec. 3.2.1 states the PM may be responsible for hiring the CM (paid by him or directly by the Owner on salary or percentage of construction cost) or serving as CM himself. (Source: SPP Document 206, Sec. 3.2.1)

q: What is the overall objective of Project Management (PM) as described in SPP 206?
o: To reduce the number of team members on a project
To eliminate the need for a Construction Manager
To have control over time, cost, and quality relative to the construction of a project
To replace the Architect's design authority
n: Sec. 1.2.2 states PM involves management activities over and above normal A&E services, with the overall objective of controlling time, cost, and quality relative to the project's construction. (Source: SPP Document 206, Sec. 1.2.2)

q: How is the Project Manager compensated under SPP 206?
o: By the Contractor directly, never by the Owner
On a fixed lump sum set by the PRC
On a percentage basis, as described in the Architect's Guidelines
n: Sec. 4.1 states the Project Manager is compensated on a percentage basis, as shall be described in the Architect's Guidelines. (Source: SPP Document 206, Sec. 4.1)

q: Under SPP 206, when does an engagement constitute Project Management (PM) rather than plain Comprehensive Architectural Services?
o: Whenever the Architect uses more than one consultant
Only when a foreign Owner is involved
When the Owner hires an Architect or a firm specifically to coordinate the whole range of Comprehensive Architectural Services
Whenever construction cost exceeds a fixed peso threshold
n: Sec. 1.2.1 provides that when the Owner hires an Architect or firm to coordinate the whole range of CAS, this constitutes Project Management (PM). (Source: SPP Document 206, Sec. 1.2.1)

q: Under the Team Approach, which team member makes decisions on the project and assures that funds are available to complete it?
n: Sec. 3.2.2(d) states the Owner makes decisions on the project and assures that funds are available to complete it. (Source: SPP Document 206, Sec. 3.2.2(d))

q: Regular Design Services, cross-referenced in SPP 206 to SPP Document 202, are broken down into how many phases?
n: Sec. 2.1.2 lists six phases: Project Definition, Schematic Design, Design Development, Contract Documents, Bidding or Negotiation, and Construction Phase. (Source: SPP Document 206, Sec. 2.1.2)

q: Situational: An Architect acting as Project Manager (PM) for a project also personally performs the Regular Design Services for the same project. How should he be compensated for the design work under SPP 206?
o: He may not accept any separate fee for the design services
He must bill the design fee to the Contractor instead of the Owner
He shall be compensated separately for the design services, as stipulated in SPP Document 202
The design fee is automatically waived as part of the PM percentage
n: Sec. 4.2 provides that if the Architect as PM also performs regular design services for the same project, he shall be compensated separately for these services as stipulated in SPP Document 202. (Source: SPP Document 206, Sec. 4.2)

q: SPP Document 206 is issued as part of the Implementing Rules and Regulations (IRR) of which law?
n: The document's header identifies it as 'Part of the IRR of R.A. No. 9266,' the Architecture Act of 2004. (Source: SPP Document 206, Header)

q: Which of the following is one of the six phases of Regular Design Services listed in SPP 206?
n: Design Development Phase is phase (c) under Regular Design Services (SPP Document 202); the other choices belong to Pre-Design, Post-Construction, and Specialized Services respectively. (Source: SPP Document 206, Sec. 2.1.2)

q: Per SPP 206 Sec. 3.2.1, how may the Fulltime Supervisor on a project be engaged?
o: Either as a staff member of the PM, or hired directly by the Owner
Only as a sub-consultant of the Engineer
Only through a government procurement process
Only as a direct employee of the Contractor
n: Sec. 3.2.1 states the Fulltime Supervisor can either be a staff member of the PM or hired directly by the Owner. (Source: SPP Document 206, Sec. 3.2.1)

q: Which SPP document specifically governs the Pre-Design Services referenced within SPP 206's scope of Comprehensive Architectural Services?
n: Sec. 2.1.1 cross-references Pre-Design Services to SPP Document 201. (Source: SPP Document 206, Sec. 2.1.1)

q: Is the Architect expected to personally perform all the services that make up CAS?
o: Only licensed sub-architects may perform any delegated service
Yes, personal performance of every service is mandatory
Only the Post-Construction Services may be delegated
No — the Architect is not expected to perform all the services; rather he acts as the agent of the Client in procuring and coordinating the necessary services
n: Sec. 1.1.4 states the Architect is not expected to perform all the services; he acts as the Client's agent in procuring and coordinating the services a project requires. (Source: SPP Document 206, Sec. 1.1.4)

q: Under the Team Approach described in SPP 206 Sec. 3.2.2, which member(s) have prime responsibility for the plan/design of the project?
o: The Architect and the Specialist Consultants (SCs)
n: Sec. 3.2.2(a) states the Architect and the Specialist Consultants (SCs) have prime responsibility for the plan/design of the project. (Source: SPP Document 206, Sec. 3.2.2(a))

q: Comprehensive Architectural Services (CAS), as defined in SPP 206, refers to the range of professional services covering which groups?
o: Design-Build and Construction Management Services only
Pre-design, Regular Design, Specialized Architectural, Construction, and Post-Construction Services
Only Regular Design and Construction Services
Pre-design, Bidding, and Post-Construction Services only
n: SPP 206 Sec. 1.1.2 defines CAS as the range of services covering Pre-design Services, Regular Design Services, Specialized Architectural Services, Construction Services, and Post-Construction Services — five groups in all. (Source: SPP Document 206, Sec. 1.1.2)

q: Under the Team Approach, who is responsible for his own men and equipment and for the delivery of the project?
n: Sec. 3.2.2(c) states the Contractor is responsible for his men and equipment and the delivery of the project. (Source: SPP Document 206, Sec. 3.2.2(c))

q: Which of the following is listed as a Specialized Architectural Service under SPP 206?
n: Forensic Architecture is one of the Specialized Architectural Services in Sec. 2.1.3 (item m). Contract Documents Phase is a Regular Design phase, Site Selection and Analysis is a Pre-Design service, and Post-Construction Evaluation is a Post-Construction service. (Source: SPP Document 206, Sec. 2.1.3)
